datasetDescription: Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity Intrusion Detection System 2017 dataset. Simulates 5 days of realistic network traffic with seven labelled classes (Benign + six attack families).
featureCategories: Flag counts (SYN, ACK, FIN, RST, PSH, URG)

attackClasses.name: Benign Traffic
attackClasses.description: Normal, legitimate network activity including web browsing, DNS lookups, email, internal banking applications, and inter-branch VPN traffic.

attackClasses.name: Brute Force
attackClasses.description: Credential-guessing attacks against SSH, FTP, or web login endpoints. Typically many failed authentication attempts from a single source IP range.

attackClasses.name: Denial of Service
attackClasses.description: Single-source resource exhaustion designed to overwhelm a target service (CPU, memory, or connection table). Slowloris, SYN flood, and HTTP slow POST variants.

attackClasses.name: Web Attack
attackClasses.description: Application-layer attacks: SQL injection, cross-site scripting, path traversal, and command injection delivered through HTTP parameters or headers.

attackClasses.name: Infiltration
attackClasses.description: Low-and-slow lateral movement: an attacker already inside the perimeter enumerates internal hosts, escalates privileges, and exfiltrates data in small bursts.

attackClasses.name: Botnet
attackClasses.description: Hosts compromised and controlled by a C2 server. Behaviours include periodic beaconing, port scanning the internet, and spam or click-fraud payloads.

attackClasses.name: DDoS
attackClasses.description: Multi-source amplification or reflection attack (DNS, NTP, LDAP) or a large coordinated botnet producing packets far exceeding any single uplink capacity.

scopeNotes: This is a six-bank simulated environment on CICIDS2017 labels; values illustrate workflow, not production results.
We do not handle fraud, mule-account detection, transaction analytics, or blockchain use cases.
Only the network-intrusion detection task is in scope for this demonstration.
